mortensor

🚸CAUTION: This package is vibe-coded ✨. Use at your own risk🚸

Cause-Specific Coherent Ensemble Mortality Forecasting including Tensor Decomposition Approaches

mortensor is a modular R package for forecasting age-specific mortality rates across population strata (e.g. sex × deprivation quintile) and causes of death. It combines Tucker tensor decomposition with compositional data analysis, ensemble time-series methods, and rigorous uncertainty quantification.

Why mortensor?

Mortality data are inherently multi-way: rates vary by age, period, and population group simultaneously. Univariate methods (Lee-Carter, ARIMA per series) ignore this structure. mortensor models the full age × period × group array jointly via Tucker3 decomposition, extracting low-rank patterns that generalise better out-of-sample.

Key design goals:

  • Stratified by default — designed for sex × deprivation (or similar) cross-classifications, not just aggregate data
  • Ensemble-first — automatic model comparison and inverse-MASE weighting over Tucker3, Lee-Carter, FDM, StMoMo, ARIMA, ETS, and RWD
  • Coherent multi-cause — WLS reconciliation and Tucker4-ILR ensure disease-specific forecasts sum to all-cause
  • Honest uncertainty — residual bootstrap and GAM-Bayes posterior propagation produce well-calibrated 95% prediction intervals
  • Actuarially complete — disaggregates 5-year groups to single-year ages and computes full abridged life tables

Installation 

# From GitHub
remotes::install_github("kalleEF/mortensor")

# From a local clone
devtools::install("path/to/mortensor")

Optional backends 

install.packages("demography")  # Lee-Carter and FDM models
install.packages("StMoMo")      # Stochastic mortality models
install.packages("nnls")        # NNLS ensemble stacking
install.packages("readxl")      # ONS Excel import

Quick start 

library(mortensor)

# Load the example dataset (mort_data object)
data(example_mortality)

# 1. Smooth — 2D GAM P-spline, exclude COVID years
sm <- smooth_mortality(example_mortality, method = "gam",
                       covid_years = c(2020L, 2021L))

# 2. Calibrate — compare Tucker3, Lee-Carter, FDM, ETS, ARIMA, RWD;
#    build inverse-MASE ensemble from top 3
cal <- calibrate(sm, holdout_frac = 0.2, ensemble = TRUE)
print(cal)

# 3. Forecast
fc <- forecast(cal, h = 10)

# 4. Add 95% prediction intervals (bootstrap)
fc <- add_pi(fc, n_sim = 500, method = "bootstrap")

# 5. Disaggregate to single-year ages (30–100)
fc_1yr <- disaggregate(fc, target_ages = 30:100,
                       method = "natural_gompertz")

# 6. Life expectancy (with PI bounds)
le <- life_expectancy(fc)
print(le)

# 7. Export to CSV
export(fc, dir = "results/")

Pipeline overview 

mort_data ──► smooth_mortality() ──► calibrate() ──► forecast()
                                                          │
                                                     add_pi()
                                                          │
                                                  disaggregate()
                                                          │
                                              life_expectancy() / export()

Every step returns an S3 object with print(), summary(), plot(), and export() methods.

Core features

Tensor decomposition (Tucker3)

Mortality rates mx,t,gm_{x,t,g} are arranged in a 3D array (age × year × group) and decomposed as:

𝒳≈𝒢×1𝐀×2𝐁×3𝐂\mathcal{X} \approx \mathcal{G} \times_1 \mathbf{A} \times_2 \mathbf{B} \times_3 \mathbf{C}

The temporal mode 𝐁\mathbf{B} is the only component that changes over time — its columns are forecast individually using ARIMA, ETS, or random walk with drift. Two transform strategies are provided:

  • Tucker3-CoDa: CLR transform on death shares (compositional, bounded)
  • Tucker3-Direct: log-transform on mortality rates (simpler, often competitive for all-cause)

Ranks (RA,RB,RC)(R_A, R_B, R_C) and the time-series method are selected by rolling-origin cross-validation or BIC/AIC.

Model ensemble

calibrate() evaluates all available models on a holdout period and builds an ensemble via inverse-MASE weighting:

Model Backend
Tucker3-CoDa rTensor + compositions
Tucker3-Direct rTensor
Lee-Carter demography
FDM demography
StMoMo APC StMoMo
ARIMA per series forecast
ETS (damped) forecast
Random walk + drift —

Prediction intervals

Two methods are available via add_pi():

Method Description Speed
"bootstrap" Residual resampling + ARIMA/ETS simulation Fast (seconds)
"gam_bayes" GAM posterior draws → full pipeline re-forecast Slower (minutes)

Both produce mx_lower / mx_upper / mx_median arrays and a full sims array for custom quantile extraction.

Age disaggregation

Three methods disaggregate abridged (5-year) age groups to single years:

Method Interpolation Old-age extrapolation
"hyman_kannisto" Monotone Hermite spline Kannisto logistic
"natural_gompertz" Natural cubic spline Gompertz log-linear
"gam" 2D GAM (age × year) Blended parametric tail

All methods enforce the group-mean constraint (mean of single-year rates matches the original 5-year grouped rate).

Multi-cause coherence

For cause-of-death forecasting, two coherence strategies are available:

WLS reconciliation (reconcile()): Forecast each cause independently, then adjust via weighted least squares so that diseases sum to all-cause. Works with any per-cause model.

Tucker4-ILR (run_coherent_forecast()): Model cause shares jointly in a 4D tensor via ILR-transformed simplex coordinates. Coherence is guaranteed by construction.

Scoring rules

mortensor implements all major proper scoring rules for forecast evaluation:

Metric Function Type
Combined MASE compute_mase_combined() Point
Cell MASE compute_mase_array() Point
Trend MASE compute_mase_group_trend() Point
RMSE (log) compute_rmse_log() Point
CRPS (empirical) compute_crps_empirical() Probabilistic
CRPS (Gaussian) compute_crps_gaussian() Probabilistic
Interval score compute_interval_score_array() Probabilistic
WIS compute_wis() Probabilistic
Log-score compute_log_score_gaussian() Probabilistic

Batch pipelines

For end-to-end processing without interactive inspection:

# Single cause
config <- mort_config(cause_label = "All causes", forecast_h = 10,
                      n_sim = 500, disagg_method = "natural_gompertz")
result <- run_forecast(data, config)

# Multi-cause with WLS reconciliation
shared <- mort_shared_config(output_dir = "results/", forecast_h = 10)
result <- run_reconciled_forecast(disease_configs, all_cause_config, shared)

# Multi-cause Tucker4-ILR (coherent by construction)
result <- run_coherent_forecast(disease_configs, all_cause_config, shared)
